rules:
DECK: {deck_size} cards, used only for their values: {joker_count} Jokers worth {joker_value}; {copies_per_value_1_to_9} each of values 1 to 9 (Ace = 1); {ten_value_cards} cards worth {ten_value} (10s, Jacks, Queens, Kings). Suits are ignored.

STATE: You have {slots_per_player} private slots c1, c2, c3; each holds one card value or is empty ({empty_slot_code}). Your hand total H is the sum of your non-empty slots. Penalty totals are public and start at {initial_penalty}. The table shows the round (1 to {max_rounds}), the priority seat (seat 1 in round 1), the draw pile size (its order is hidden), the OFFER ROW (an ordered public list of cards) and the DEAD PILE (every card that has left play this hand).

EACH ROUND:
1. NEW HAND. If a new hand is due: all {deck_size} cards are shuffled into the draw pile, all slots and the dead pile are emptied, each player in seat order is dealt {cards_dealt_per_player} cards into c1, c2, c3 (told privately), and the next card is turned face up as the offer row ({initial_offer_row_length} card at position 1).
2. The offer row with positions, the dead pile, the draw pile size, the priority seat and everyone's card count are announced.
3. CHOICES. Everyone answers at the same moment, privately: (a) action: YANIV, DRAW or TAKE; (b) take position: 1 to the length of the offer row (used only for TAKE); (c) shed slot: 1, 2 or 3. If your chosen shed slot is empty, your lowest-numbered non-empty slot is used instead.
4. YANIV CHECK. A YANIV is valid only if your H is {yaniv_threshold} or less. If it is valid you are a caller. If it is not, it is announced as invalid and you are treated as DRAW for the rest of the round.
5. If at least one valid YANIV was made, no cards move this round and a showdown follows (go to step 10). If none was made, steps 6 to 9 happen.
6. SHED. Each player removes the card in their shed slot, and every other slot of theirs holding the same value is also removed (a pair sheds two cards, a triple three). Those extra slots stay empty for the rest of the hand. Every player's shed values are announced.
7. TAKE. TAKE players are resolved in seat order starting at the priority seat and wrapping around. Each receives the offer-row card at their take position if no earlier player has claimed it, and places it in their shed slot; who took which card is announced. If the card was already claimed, that player becomes DRAW instead.
8. DRAW. In the same order, each DRAW player takes the top card of the draw pile into their shed slot, told only to them; the drawn value is never announced and the draw pile shrinks by 1 per draw.
9. ROW UPDATE. Offer-row cards not taken go to the dead pile. The new offer row is every card shed in step 6, in seat order from seat 1, and in slot order within a player. Card counts and the draw pile size are announced.
10. SHOWDOWN happens if a valid YANIV was made this round, or the draw pile holds fewer cards than there are players after step 9, or this is round {max_rounds}. All hands are revealed. With valid callers: M is the lowest H among callers, N the lowest H among non-callers (N = {no_noncaller_n} if everyone called). A caller scores 0 if their H equals M and M is less than N; otherwise they score H + {asaf_penalty} (Asaf). A non-caller scores 0 if their H is less than or equal to M; otherwise they score H. With no valid caller: every player with the lowest H scores 0 and the others score their H. Scores are added to penalty totals, all totals are announced, and the next round begins a fresh hand and a fresh shuffle. Without a showdown the hand continues next round.
11. The priority seat passes to the next seat, wrapping from the last seat to seat 1.
12. END. The match ends after any showdown that leaves some penalty total at {end_penalty} or more, or after round {max_rounds}; otherwise play continues.

There is no discussion. When the match ends, the lowest penalty total wins; players tied for the lowest share the win.
